text:
The Islanders and Kings both arrive stuck. New York is winless in four (0-2-2) after a 3-2 shootout loss at San Jose that ended the Sharks' five-game winless run, and it's missing Matias Maccelli, Ryan Pulock and Calum Ritchie. Los Angeles is 2-3-0 in its last five after a 0-3 loss to Nashville, where Juuse Saros stopped all 30 shots. The Kings won the first meeting 3-2 in overtime on Oct 22.

At five on five the teams are close: the Islanders have 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and the Kings 51%. Los Angeles has been better lately, with 59% of the expected goals over its last five, yet it lost three of them. The special-teams matchup to watch is the Kings' power play (0.79 expected goals a game) against an Islanders penalty kill that allows 0.90. New York also takes 4.8 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Ilya Sorokin is +8.2 goals saved above expected this season, while projected Darcy Kuemper is at -5.0.

For New York, Bo Horvat is our top pick at 38% to score, and with Maccelli out he's moved beside Cizikas and Holmstrom. Matthew Schaefer, the 2025 first overall pick, plays his 100th game and is 70% for a point. For the Kings, Adrian Kempe is 37% to score. Our under-the-radar picks are Corey Perry (21% to score), whose 3.6 expected goals in his last 10 games are better than 99% of depth forwards, and Quinton Byfield, at 50% for a point because his line creates chances. Both are players to watch, not locks.
